sentences.text: New books preserve 144 names after a village lost its future in seconds.
sentences.why: Professional narration with natural intonation and pacing.

sentences.text: On 21 October 1966, a massive coal waste tip collapsed onto Aberfan.
sentences.why: Good emotional delivery and clear pronunciation.

sentences.text: 116 children and 28 adults lost their lives in the disaster.
sentences.why: Maintains a steady, engaging documentary tone.

sentences.text: Will the National Library of Wales protect these pages?
sentences.why: Slightly elevated pitch for the question, well-executed.

sentences.text: Time wears down the original Aberfan Book of Remembrance, but fresh copies are needed.
sentences.why: Natural pauses and good emphasis on key words.

sentences.text: The National Library of Wales finished new copies ahead of July 2026.
sentences.why: Clear articulation and steady professional flow.

sentences.text: Aberfan Memorial Charity chair Davies guards the community's history now.
At 68 years old, Davies protects the village's memory.
144 names remain protected in fresh leather and ink.
sentences.why: Strong concluding sentence with good resonance.
